lliban-el-hijo-del-trueno: Whenever the scene explicitly calls for the servant/helper, he is a DISTINCT young adult: bare head with short straight black hair, plain OCHRE-BROWN short ruana, gray trousers, no white shoulder bag. NEVER give the helper Lliban's brimmed hat, sage-green ruana and ivory bag. Lliban retains exactly those reference features. Only show the helper if named in the shot. This reversible editorial costume distinction prevents mistaken identity. When the shot explicitly names doctors (medicos), show ONLY the two doctors from entrada: both wear muted green ruanas, one a plain golden-yellow hat, the other a gray brimmed hat. This is before Lliban grows up. The ochre-clothed bareheaded helper is ABSENT from birth scenes. Lliban is only a wrapped baby when explicitly requested.
lliban-y-juan-chiracol: STRICT IDENTITIES: Juan Chiracol wears a BLUE RUANA, GRAY TROUSERS, NO HAT, uncovered shoulder-length dark hair, ivory bag. Lliban wears a GREEN RUANA, DARK TROUSERS and a BRIMMED HAT. If this shot names Juan alone, Lliban is absent and NO HAT is allowed. If it names Lliban alone, Juan is absent. Never swap their costumes or destinations.
chauteh: When named in the shot: CHAUTEH has LONG jagged black hair, DARK OLIVE GREEN ragged layered ruana, GRAY trousers, NO WHITE BAG, NO HAT. Only Chauteh is affected by his later captivity and eye loss, strictly at the stated scene.
